Well, thank you for seeing me. Honestly, what brings me in is... well, it’s my head. It just feels so terribly cloudy lately, like there's a thick fog in there. I manage community associations—HOAs, condo buildings, that sort of thing—and I’ve been doing it a long time. I’m 64, and I’ve always prided myself on being sharp, especially since I had to work my way up from the bottom, not having gone past the eighth grade, you know? You have to be quick on your feet in this business to keep the residents happy. 

But lately... I don't know, I'll be sitting at my desk, and I just stare at a board packet. Just stare right at the pages. Or I’ll get a vendor email—like the other day, the landscaping company emailed asking if we wanted the winter mulch put down on Tuesday or Thursday, which is a nothing question, right?—and I just cannot decide. I mean, these are simple, everyday things! I used to handle them so fast, just boom, boom, boom, reply sent, problem solved, moving on to the next property. But now, it’s like my brain just stalls out. I’ll read the same sentence from a vendor over and over, and I just sit there with this cloudy feeling, completely unable to make a basic choice about mulch or gate repairs or whatever it is, and before I know it I've wasted an hour just trying to answer one simple question...

Sleep? No, my sleep is completely fine. I've always been a good sleeper, honestly. You have to be in this business, you really need your rest to deal with people all day. Memory? Well, let me think about that. I wouldn't call it a memory problem, exactly, no. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Focus? Well, it really depends on what you mean by focus. If you mean, do I get distracted and wander off to go water the office plants or make a cup of coffee every five minutes? No, not at all. I can sit at my desk and look at one single piece of paper for an hour straight. 

But... well, that's exactly what I keep coming back to, Doctor. That is the entire reason what brings me in today. I can focus my eyes on something, sure, but my head just feels so incredibly cloudy that all that focus doesn't actually do me any good. 

Like I was saying before, I will literally just sit there and stare at a board packet. Or I'll open up a vendor email—say, from the landscaping company wanting to know if we're doing the premium dyed mulch or the standard cedar bark this spring, which usually takes me two seconds to answer because I know the operating budget for that property inside and out—and I just stare at the screen. I am completely focused on it, but I cannot decide even simple things that I used to handle so fast. I just sit there looking at the words, trapped in that awful fog, completely unable to make a choice. 

So, yes, I suppose I stay on that one single task for a very extended period of time, but I don't actually get anywhere with it! I just spin my wheels. Do you see what I mean? It's not that my attention is jumping all over the place, it's just this heavy cloud in my head that absolutely refuses to let me process the thing I'm focusing on.

Well, yes, exactly. I feel like I'm just a ghost haunting my own life right now, to be perfectly honest. I know we're sort of circling around the same drain here, and I know I keep harping on this, but it’s because it's the truest way I can explain what's happening to me.

Well, I haven't exactly been stepping on the scale, Doctor, because frankly, who wants to do that when they're feeling like this? But my clothes are definitely fitting a bit looser, especially around the waist on those slacks I wear to the property office. 

It's just... my eating has been completely off lately. Completely off. I know I mentioned the plain rye toast earlier, but honestly, most days I don't even finish that. It's just mindless picking, like I know I should put something in my stomach but I can't be bothered to actually make a meal or taste what I'm eating. It all just tastes like cardboard anyway. So yes, I suppose I probably have lost some weight, just because I'm practically living on coffee and tortilla scraps, which I know isn't healthy, but I just can't seem to muster the energy to care about food right now.

Well, like I was saying before... I really haven't. It's just so frustrating, Doctor. The things that usually bring me so much joy, the things that make me feel like, well, like *me*... they just don't have any appeal right now. I don't get any spark from them at all.

Well, yes, Doctor, like I was just saying a few minutes ago... it's exactly that. I just don't have the desire to do the things I used to love. It's really quite distressing to me, because those things are what make me feel like, well, like *me*.

It's like all the color has been washed out of my life, Doctor, and I'm just left with this gray, empty feeling where my interests used to be.

Energy? Well... no, I wouldn't say that. I know I said a minute ago about not having the energy for my dancing shoes, but I didn't mean it like a physical tiredness, if that makes sense. It's not like my body is worn out or I'm sleeping all day. 

I still get up right at 6:15 every single morning, regular as a clock, just like I have for the last forty years. So I'm walking, I'm moving around just fine. My body works. I'm not napping in the middle of the afternoon or dragging my feet when I do my rounds. I can still scrub my kitchen floors on my hands and knees, and I do my laundry every Thursday morning like always. The physical energy is absolutely there. I *could* physically walk down to the art gallery, or I *could* stand at the stove and chop carrots and peel potatoes for a Sunday roast. My arms and legs would do it just fine. 

It's just... I don't have the heart for it. The spirit for it is what's gone. When it comes to the things I actually *have* to do for work or just keeping the house clean, I just push through and do them, and my energy is exactly the same as it always was. It's just the fun things. I just don't want to do them. So no, I haven't noticed my actual energy dropping at all. It's just that heavy, gray feeling I was telling you about.

The funny thing is, nobody has actually complained to me. Mrs. Higgins hasn't said a word about the patio furniture, and Mr. Abernathy just waves when he walks by. Nobody has told me I ruined anything or made a mess of it. But I just *know* I did. I can feel it. I let them all down by talking too big and promising things I couldn't deliver, and I just can't shake this feeling that I'm doing a terrible job and failing everyone who relies on me.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that you no longer derive pleasure from activities that you once found enjoyable?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, Doctor, like I was just saying a few minutes ago... it's exactly that. We'd do our steps, have a good laugh, maybe complain about our joints a little bit, but it was wonderful. Now, when Tuesday rolls around, I just look at my dancing shoes in the closet and I can't even fathom putting them on. The very thought of trying to keep time with the music or make small talk just feels like climbing a mountain. There's this one little place on Main Street that always has the most beautiful watercolors, and I could spend an hour just looking at the brushstrokes and chatting with the owner, Mr. Davies. He always remembers how I like my tea if I stop in the cafe next door. But lately, I haven't even had the slightest urge to go look. I just sit in my chair at home. \n\nAnd of course, the Sunday dinners with my family. I've always been the one to cook. It's a tradition! Getting the roast just right, making sure my daughter's favorite potatoes are on the table, seeing the grandchildren's faces when I bring out a pie... that was my joy. That was how I showed them I loved them. But now, I just haven't wanted to cook Sunday food for them at all. The kitchen feels overwhelming, and the joy I used to get from feeding my family is just... gone. It's like all the color has been washed out of my life, Doctor, and I'm just left with this gray, empty feeling where my interests used to be.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you have less energy than you used to?\n\nPatient: Energy? Well... no, I wouldn't say that. I know I said a minute ago about not having the energy for my dancing shoes, but I didn't mean it like a physical tiredness, if that makes sense. It's not like my body is worn out or I'm sleeping all day. \n\nI still get up right at 6:15 every single morning, regular as a clock, just like I have for the last forty years. I make my bed, I fix my coffee—just instant, nothing fancy, I never had the schooling or the money to get into all those expensive machines they have nowadays—and I go straight down to the property office. I'm on my feet plenty, Doctor. Why, just yesterday, I walked the entire perimeter of the complex. That's all six buildings! I had to go check on the gutters behind building C because Mr. Abernathy said they were overflowing into his hydrangeas, and then I walked all the way over to the maintenance shed on the far side of the property to see if the boys had the right ladder to get up there and clean them out. \n\nSo I'm walking, I'm moving around just fine. My body works. I'm not napping in the middle of the afternoon or dragging my feet when I do my rounds. I can still scrub my kitchen floors on my hands and knees, and I do my laundry every Thursday morning like always. The physical energy is absolutely there. I *could* physically walk down to the art gallery, or I *could* stand at the stove and chop carrots and peel potatoes for a Sunday roast. My arms and legs would do it just fine. \n\nIt's just... I don't have the heart for it. The spirit for it is what's gone. When it comes to the things I actually *have* to do for work or just keeping the house clean, I just push through and do them, and my energy is exactly the same as it always was. It's just the fun things. I just don't want to do them. So no, I haven't noticed my actual energy dropping at all. It's just that heavy, gray feeling I was telling you about."
